identity.name: Burgundians
alt_names: Burgundian tribes before the Rhine kingdom

land.text: the Rhine settlement near Worms with which Cliopatria's Burgundian Kingdom row opens in 414

successors.note: The same people: the Burgundians page and the Kingdom of the Burgundians page treat the Rhine settlement of 411-413 as the start of the kingdom. Cliopatria's two rows share Wikidata Q13590051; this dossier ends at the 413 grant of land and the other row continues (notes).

capitals.name: Borbetomagus (Worms)
capitals.note: Infobox 'Capital: Borbetomagus (411-437)'; the page places the settlement 'probably near Worms' on the west bank of the Rhine. Before 411 the pages record no seat.

correction.text: Ptolemy (2nd century) places the Burgundians 'between the Suevus (probably the Oder) and Vistula rivers': the Cliopatria shape of 224 (Oder to Vistula), used for 154-290

keyframe_review.note: 611.7 km2 on Bornholm (Denmark), 154-223. The page records that early medieval writers called Bornholm 'Burgund land' but treats any link to the continental Burgundians as unproven; the 2nd-century evidence (Ptolemy) puts them between the Oder and the Vistula, which is Cliopatria's own shape from 224. No infobox area is given on the pages opened.

correction.text: the shape unchanged but for 154-290 only: Oder to Vistula, where Ptolemy has them and where in the 3rd century the Gepid king Fastida 'nearly annihilated' them near the Vistula; from 291 the Main (new keyframe burgundians_291)

keyframe_review.note: 100,279 km2 (Poland, Germany) for 224-346. The page has the main concentration possibly shifting 'west over the Oder' in the later 3rd century, Probus fighting Burgundi in 278, Burgundiones with the Alemanni attacking Gaul in 287 and a panegyric of 291 reporting Burgundians taking Alemanni farmland, and by c. 314 the Laterculus Veronensis placing them between the Alemanni and the Chatti: the east-Oder shape does not fit 291-346.

correction.text: the Main valley between the Alemanni and the Chatti: 'The Burgundians also took Alemanni farmland' (291), 'the Burgunziones between the Alemanni and Chatti' (Laterculus Veronensis, c. 314), border stones of Burgundian territory (Julian, 359), allies of Valentinian against the Alemanni (369/370), 'almost 80,000 Burgundians' reaching the Rhine (373, Jerome)

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe covering Cliopatria's gap 347-406 and replacing its 291-346 Oder shape. The Kingdom of the Burgundians page, opened second, agrees: 'Before the Rhine, the Burgundians lived east of the Rhine near the Main.' The radius is a reading of 'near the Main', soft; the pages give no boundary.

correction.text: the Rhine settlement 'probably near Worms' on the west bank, Cliopatria's Burgundian Kingdom shape of 414, used for 409-413 (new keyframe burgundians_409); 407-408 the Burgundians are still on the Main (burgundians_291)

keyframe_review.note: 9,094 km2 at 47.6-48.9 N, 407-409: the Upper Rhine near Strasbourg and Basel, about 100 km south of Worms. The page has 'The Burgundians of Gundahar crossed the Rhine into Roman Gaul before 409' (the Burgundians page says c. 406) and the settlement 'near Borbetomagus, probably near Worms'; neither page puts them on the Upper Rhine.

correction.text: the west bank of the Rhine around Borbetomagus, 'probably near Worms': 'Gundahar is granted land on the western bank of the Rhine by Honorius: 411' (infobox), foederati 'in 413' (text)

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria has no shape for 410-413 and its 409 shape is misplaced. Cliopatria's Burgundian Kingdom shape for 414-438 (6,880 km2) is used unchanged. The Burgundians page dates Jerome's list of peoples in Gaul to 409, Gundahar at Mundiacum proclaiming Jovinus to 411 and Honorius' grant of land near the Rhine to 413 (Prosper).

region.text: between the Suevus (probably the Oder) and the Vistula

ledger.note: 154: Ptolemy places the Burgundians between the Oder and the Vistula. The page gives the 2nd century and the rivers, not a year; 154 is Cliopatria's. Pliny (1st century) lists 'Burgodiones' among the Vandili without a location.

291: the Burgundian centre moves west. 'The Burgundians' main concentration may have shifted west over the Oder' in the later 3rd century (the page is hedged and gives no year); a panegyric of 291 has the Goths 'utterly destroyed' the Burgundians. The year is a bridge to the Alemanni gain below.

291: the Burgundians take Alemanni farmland. 'Panegyric 11 says the Goths utterly destroyed the Burgundians during Maximian's reign. The Burgundians also took Alemanni farmland.' The page does not name the district; the Main valley is the reading of the c. 314 Laterculus Veronensis, which has them between the Alemanni and the Chatti. The Kingdom of Alamannia row (462-731) is far later.

region.text: the Main valley east of the Rhine, left in the crossing

ledger.note: 409: the Burgundians cross the Rhine and leave the Main. 'The Burgundians of Gundahar crossed the Rhine into Roman Gaul before 409' (Kingdom page; the Burgundians page has c. 406 and lists them in Jerome's 409 passage). The pages do not say who held the Main afterwards.

region.text: the west bank of the Rhine near Worms

ledger.note: 409: Burgundians are among the peoples who have entered Roman Gaul. Jerome (409) lists them, Gundahar is at Mundiacum proclaiming Jovinus in 411 (Olympiodorus); the pages give the Rhine crossing and Worms as the 'traditional' site, not a boundary.

region.text: the west bank of the Rhine near Worms

ledger.note: 413: Honorius recognises the Burgundian settlement. 'Honorius gave the Burgundians part of Gaul near the Rhine' (Prosper, 413); the Kingdom page's infobox has the grant at 411 and its text 'accepted as Roman foederati' after 413.

region.text: part of Gaul near the Rhine, traditionally Worms

ledger.note: 413: the Burgundians receive land in Gaul near the Rhine as foederati. The page says Worms is only the traditional location.

413: the Burgundians become the federate Kingdom of the Burgundians. The Kingdom page treats Gundahar's Rhine settlement as the kingdom's first phase ('Borbetomagus (411-437)'); Cliopatria's Burgundian Kingdom row opens in 414 and carries the story on.

wars.name: Probus's campaign against the Burgundi and Vandals
wars.outcome: Zosimus says Probus defeated the Burgundi and Vandals near a river (the Lech, if the page's guess is right).
wars.note: A raid defeated on Roman ground; no border moved.

wars.name: Maximian's defence of Gaul against the Burgundiones and Alemanni
wars.outcome: The Burgundiones and Alemanni attacked Gaul and were defeated by Maximian (reported in a panegyric of 289).

wars.name: Gothic defeat of the Burgundians (panegyric of 291)
wars.outcome: The Goths 'utterly destroyed' the Burgundians in Maximian's reign; the Burgundians also took Alemanni farmland.
wars.note: The page does not say where; it dates the panegyric 291.

wars.name: Valentinian's Alemannic campaign with Burgundian allies
wars.outcome: Valentinian enlisted the Burgundians against the Alemanni and their king Macrianus; Ammianus says they 'knew that they are descendants of the Romans from ancient times'.
wars.note: An alliance, not a border change.

certainty.note: Tribal territory known from Ptolemy, a few panegyrics and the Laterculus Veronensis; the Rhine settlement near Worms is a traditional site, not a surveyed one.

sources.title: Burgundians
sources.note: Ptolemy, the Oder-Vistula homeland, the 3rd-4th century wars, the Main, the Rhine crossing and Honorius' grant (to 413).

sources.title: Kingdom of the Burgundians
sources.note: Gundahar's Rhine settlement near Worms, infobox capital 411-437, crossing 'before 409', relation to the earlier Burgundians.

notes:
Cliopatria's 'Burgundians' (154-409) and 'Burgundian Kingdom' (414-660) share Wikidata Q13590051. They are one people, but the first row is a tribe outside the empire and the second a federate kingdom inside it, and the brief assigns burgundian-kingdom to another part; this dossier therefore stops at the 413 grant of land (a dissolve event at confidence 2, successor burgundian-kingdom); the orchestrator may merge the two under 'burgundians' if it prefers one state (the huns dossier of this batch merged its two Q45813 rows, see its notes, so the rule applied differently there). Cliopatria's 410-413 gap is closed by the new keyframe burgundians_409; the Burgundian Kingdom row opens in 414.

Cliopatria shapes corrected: the Bornholm shape of 154-223 is not supported (the page treats the link as unproven; Ptolemy has the Oder-Vistula); the Oder-Vistula shape runs to 346 although the pages put the Burgundians on the Alemanni frontier from 278-291 and between the Alemanni and Chatti by c. 314 (new keyframe 291-408 on the Main, soft); the 407-409 shape on the Upper Rhine is 100 km from Worms. The date of the westward move is a bridge (confidence 1); the Burgundians page says only that the main concentration 'may have shifted west over the Oder' in the later 3rd century. The page budget was two pages and no further page was opened: the c. 406 Rhine crossing (Burgundians page) against 'before 409' (Kingdom page) is unresolved.

No infobox area exists on either page, so the factor-of-two check was impossible. No capital is recorded before 411; no ruler list is given (Gundahar appears only from 411). Counterparts needing dossiers: the Alemanni before 462 (Kingdom of Alamannia starts 462), the Gepids before 510. Gazetteer: all names resolved.
